sites.current_behavior: Returns `<root>/.agents/skills` (project) or `~/.agents/skills` (global). It is the SINGLE resolution point for the Master, and 9 call sites treat its result as simultaneously (a) where the Master lives, (b) the SKILLS-DIR that classify compares agent read/write paths against, and (c) the npx-compatible layout root. Callers: manager/skill.rs:1400 (universal_install_prep), install_fetched.rs:422 + :628 (materialize_universal_master), rename.rs:703/:808/:927, transfer.rs:1739 (protected_targets), cli/commands/coverage.rs:30, cli/commands/doctor.rs:546, cli/commands/source.rs:897, api/routes/coverage.rs:41.
sites.breaks_how: The three roles fuse today only because storage == authorization. Splitting Master (`.agent-hub`) from Referrer root (`.agents/skills`) makes one function have to answer two different questions, and every caller silently gets the Master answer where some of them want the Referrer answer (doctor.rs:546 sweeps the master dir for orphans; transfer.rs:1739 builds the protect set; cli/check's `--write-result` name guard keys on `.agents/skills` segments).
sites.change_needed: Return `<root>/.agent-hub` / `~/.agent-hub` and rename to something that says Master (e.g. `master_store_dir`). Add a SECOND function `universal_referrer_dir()` returning `.agents/skills`, and audit each of the 9 callers for which one it wants. Fix the doc comment (it names `.agents/skills` verbatim).

sites.current_behavior: If the slot exists and `is_link`, canonicalize it; if it resolves to `master_real` return `AlreadyLinked` WITHOUT rewriting the stored target; otherwise `Conflict`. There is no repoint path — `Linker::link` can only create into an empty slot.
sites.breaks_how: Migration rule #5 turns `<root>/.agents/skills/foo` from a real dir into a symlink to `../../.agent-hub/foo`. Existing per-agent referrers created with `LinkTarget::Relative` (e.g. `<root>/.claude/skills/foo -> ../../.agents/skills/foo`, exactly the shape pinned by mod.rs:1140) now resolve through TWO hops. `canonicalize` follows both, so `Linker::link` sees a link that resolves to the master and returns `AlreadyLinked` — forever. Every later install, `source sync`, and rename-relink leaves the two-hop chain intact. The moment the user does the promised "手動收緊" and deletes `.agents/skills/foo`, claude/zed/windsurf/... dangle, and nothing in aghub ever noticed. Silent, and it destroys skills for agents that were never named in the tightening command.
sites.change_needed: Migration must not rely on `Linker::link` to repair chains: it must `read_link` every per-agent referrer, and for any whose stored target routes through `.agents/skills`, `Linker::unlink` + relink straight at `.agent-hub/<name>` (manager/skill.rs:1472 `universal_relink_agents` is the existing unlink-then-link shape to reuse). Separately, consider having `Linker::link` compare `read_link()` (the STORED target) against the requested target, not just the canonicalized resolution, so an indirect-but-resolving link is distinguishable from a correct one.

sites.breaks_how: After the split, `canonical` is `.agent-hub/<name>` while the old on-disk master sits at `.agents/skills/<name>`. `create_dir(.agent-hub/<name>)` SUCCEEDS on an unmigrated (or partially migrated) install — the guards above are now looking at a path that has never existed. Result: the source is copied to `.agent-hub/<name>`, then `Linker::link` hits the old real directory in `.agents/skills` and reports `Conflict`, so TWO full copies sit on disk and every one of the 8 project agents keeps reading the STALE one. `created_master: true`, so a rollback deletes only the new copy and leaves the stale one authoritative. The hash-mismatch guard that exists precisely to stop adopting foreign content no longer fires.
sites.change_needed: Preflight every `NeedsLink` slot for a REAL directory (not a link) BEFORE the `create_dir` claim at mod.rs:229 — or refuse any install while an unmigrated `.agents/skills/<name>` real dir exists, pointing the user at the migration. sites.current_behavior: The prune disk set is `agent_skill_dirs_in_scope(...)` — every agent's READ dirs — scanned with `top_level_skill_dirs`, which gates on `entry.file_type().is_dir()`. `DirEntry::file_type()` does NOT follow symlinks (verified empirically: a symlink→dir returns is_dir()==false), so a referrer symlink NEVER contributes a name. Today a symlink-installed skill is nonetheless 'present' because its Master is a REAL dir at `~/.agents/skills/<name>` / `<root>/.agents/skills/<name>`, and that store is inside the read-dir set (codex/cursor/opencode/cline/warp global; 10 agents project).
sites.breaks_how: Move the Master to `.agent-hub` and nothing scans it. Every symlink-installed skill's folder name disappears from `disk`, so `skill_present_on_disk` is false for EVERY key → the first prune wipes the whole scope's lock. `prune_lock_for_scope` is called unconditionally by `RemovalOutcome::commit` (removal.rs:1092), i.e. by every executed `delete`, plus `prune-lock --yes` and the API. Result: delete one skill, lose the source/ref/hash provenance for all of them; `check`, `source list/diff`, `apply-update` then report nothing installed. Completely silent — the prune is reported as a success with a long `pruned` list nobody reads.

checks.scenario: Claim 1 — `npx skills list` / `listInstalledSkills`: is a symlinked Master listed, and is the displayed path right?
checks.evidence: Read + ran. `listInstalledSkills` (installer.ts:1076-1310) scans `getCanonicalSkillsDir` (installer.ts:1124 → `<base>/.agents/skills`, constants.ts:1-2) and each agent dir; the entry filter is `isDirEntryOrSymlinkToDir` (installer.ts:1173 → :85-96), which `stat()`s and therefore follows the symlink; `SKILL.md` is then reached with `stat` (installer.ts:1179), which also follows. Empirical: fixture `proj/.agent-hub/foo` + `proj/.agents/skills/foo -> ../../.agent-hub/foo` + `proj/.claude/skills/foo -> ../../.agent-hub/foo`; `listInstalledSkills({global:false,cwd:proj})` returned foo with 10 agents. So it IS listed. Two problems. (a) `path` and `canonicalPath` are both set to `skillDir` verbatim (installer.ts:1205-1206, 1297-1298) — no `realpath` anywhere in the function — so `npx skills list` and `--json` report `.agents/skills/foo`, the Referrer, never `.agent-hub/foo`, the physical Master. (b) The second fixture skill `withheld` (present only at `proj/.agent-hub/withheld/SKILL.md`, no `.agents/skills` link) did NOT appear in the output at all — `.agent-hub` is scanned by nothing, so every deliberately-withheld skill is invisible to `list` while still living in the lock.
checks.consequence: Under the decided migration (link created for every existing install) `list` keeps working on day one, so this reads as a pass. But (i) the path column now points at a link, not the copy — a user who edits the printed path edits the Master through a link they were not told about; (ii) once withholding actually starts, `list` under-reports vs. the lock with no diagnostic; (iii) after any npx write verb (see claims 4/5) `list` shows ONE row whose `agents` array mixes agents reading `.agents/skills/foo` (new bytes) and agents reading `.agent-hub/foo` (old bytes) — the row asserts a sameness that no longer holds.
checks.mitigation: Accept (a) as cosmetic. For (b)/(c): treat `npx skills list` as no longer authoritative about aghub state and stop citing it as the interop smoke test; aghub's own `doctor --verify-links` must be the check. If parity of the printed path matters, aghub should not withhold silently — surface withheld skills in `aghub skills list` with an explicit marker so the discrepancy against `npx skills list` is expected rather than discovered.

checks.scenario: Claim 2 — `computeSkillFolderHash` over a symlinked Master: same digest as over a physical dir? any `relative(baseDir, …)` skew?
checks.evidence: Read + ran. `computeSkillFolderHash` (local-lock.ts:117-132) calls `collectFiles(skillDir, skillDir, files)`; `collectFiles` (local-lock.ts:134-156) uses `readdir(currentDir, {withFileTypes:true})` at :139 — a path resolution, so it follows the top-level symlink — and builds `relativePath` at :151 as `relative(baseDir, fullPath)` where `fullPath = join(currentDir, entry.name)` (:143). Both `baseDir` and `fullPath` are built from the SAME unresolved string (`.agents/skills/foo`), and nothing in the function calls `realpath`/`lstat` on the base, so the relative path can never skew. Nested symlinks are still skipped (`isDirectory()` false at :145 AND `isFile()` false at :149 → the entry falls through both branches), matching the aghub contract. Empirical: identical fixture content laid out three ways gave one digest — via symlink `84f25e7e…bf50`, via the real `.agent-hub` dir `84f25e7e…bf50`, via a plain unlinked dir `84f25e7e…bf50` (EQUAL: true).
checks.consequence: None. `computedHash` in `skills-lock.json` stays byte-identical whether npx hashes the Referrer or aghub hashes the Master, so lock comparison keeps agreeing across tools. One residual: if a `.agents/skills/<name>` link is ever left dangling (Master gone), `readdir` at :139 throws ENOENT and the rejection propagates — `sync.ts:203` calls it un-wrapped inside the up-to-date loop, so `experimental_sync` would abort. Not reachable from the migration plan, which never leaves a dangling link.
checks.mitigation: No change needed. Keep `crates/skill/tests/hash_parity_golden.rs` as-is — it still pins the right algorithm. Add one aghub-side invariant: never create a `.agents/skills/<name>` Referrer before its `.agent-hub/<name>` Master exists, and remove the Referrer before the Master, so no dangling link can reach npx.

checks.scenario: Claim 3 (HIGHEST PRIORITY — data loss) — `npx skills remove`: does it unlink the Referrer or delete through into `.agent-hub`? how does its reference counting behave?
checks.evidence: Read + ran, twice. NO DATA LOSS: `rm(canonicalPath,{recursive:true,force:true})` (remove.ts:231) and the per-agent `rm` (remove.ts:203) do not follow — direct probe on Node v26.8.1 with `.agents/skills/foo -> ../../.agent-hub/foo`: after `fs.rm(link,{recursive:true,force:true})` → "master still there? true / link gone? true" (`fs.rm` dispatches on `lstat`, so a symlink is unlinked, never descended). BUT the command is dead on arrival: discovery runs through `scanDir` (remove.ts:45-58) whose ONLY filter is `if (entry.isDirectory())` at :49 — NOT `isDirEntryOrSymlinkToDir`, which upstream itself documents as false-for-symlinks at installer.ts:84. Ran the real `removeCommand(["foo"],{yes:true})` against the symlinked-Master fixture: `Found 0 unique installed skill(s)` → `No skills found to remove.`, and afterwards `.agents/skills/foo`, `.claude/skills/foo` and `.agent-hub/foo/SKILL.md` all still existed. Baseline control on today's layout (real dir at `.agents/skills/foo` + `.claude/skills/foo` symlink): `Found 1 unique installed skill(s)` → `Successfully removed 1 skill(s)`, both paths gone. Clean regression, caused by this change. `scanDir` runs at remove.ts:60-76, BEFORE `--all` (:100), before name matching (:102-110) and before the `-a` agent list (:131-139), so every spelling bails at :81-84 or :107-110. Reference counting (remove.ts:217-228) is unreachable in this state; when it is reachable it is also blind to `.agent-hub` — `getInstallPath` (installer.ts:565-587) returns the canonical `.agents/skills/<name>` for every universal agent (installer.ts:127-129), so it counts the Referrer, never an aghub Referrer that points into `.agent-hub` from an agent npx does not model.
checks.consequence: `npx skills remove <name>` becomes a silent no-op for EVERY aghub-installed skill — not just withheld ones, because the migration plan links all of them. Exit status stays 0 and the message is the friendly "No skills found to remove", so a user or script reads it as "already clean" rather than "the tool cannot see your skills". Same gate also neuters `update`'s deleted-upstream cleanup (update.ts:249-282 → `removeCommand` at :276): it prompts about a deleted skill, the user says yes, and nothing is removed. No data is destroyed; the interop guarantee "npx can uninstall what aghub installed" is destroyed.
checks.mitigation: Cannot be fixed on the aghub side without keeping `.agents/skills/<name>` a real directory, which is the whole point of the change. Two honest options: (1) accept and document — `npx skills remove` no longer manages aghub-installed skills; state it in the npx-skills-contract skill and in the migration release notes, and make `aghub skill delete` the only supported removal. (2) Upstream a one-line fix to remove.ts:49 (`entry.isDirectory() || entry.isSymbolicLink()`, or reuse `isDirEntryOrSymlinkToDir`) and gate the interop claim on that version. Do NOT ship the change describing removal as "unaffected" — there is a reproducible before/after.

checks.scenario: Claim 4 — `npx skills update` / `check` against a lock entry with no `.agents/skills` copy: does it re-materialize the Master and cancel the withhold?
checks.evidence: Read. PROJECT scope: `updateProjectSkills` (update.ts:487-648) takes its worklist from `skills-lock.json` alone (`getProjectSkillsForUpdate`, update.ts:224-239) and NEVER compares a hash — the clone at :578 is used only to build `discoveredPaths` for deletion detection (:581-593). Every surviving entry then hits `spawnSync(node, [cli, 'add', installUrl, '--skill', name, '-y'])` at update.ts:622-634, unconditionally, inside `for (const skill of remainingSkills)` (:604). `add` re-enters `installSkillForAgent`, whose symlink branch does `cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir)` + `copyDirectory(skill.path, canonicalDir)` at installer.ts:359-360 — i.e. it writes a real directory at `<root>/.agents/skills/<name>` whether or not one was there. GLOBAL scope: `updateGlobalSkills` (update.ts:284-485) DOES gate on a hash (:371, :406), but it first skips any entry with no `skillFolderHash` (:310-319) — and per the aghub contract aghub writes `contentHash` and leaves `skillFolderHash` empty, so aghub's global entries are reported as "Private or deleted repo" (`getSkipReason`, update.ts:176-178) and never updated. Verb surface: `check`, `update` and `upgrade` are the SAME case in cli.ts:378-381, all → `runUpdate`.

Global scope is protected only by an accident (aghub's empty `skillFolderHash`), so a future contract change that starts populating that field would open global to the same re-materialization. `sourceUrl`/`skillPath` string building (update-source.ts, whole file) is pure and touches no filesystem — not a factor.

Document in the contract skill that `npx skills update|check|upgrade` re-grants every project skill to the `.agents/skills` readers. Do not build the withhold UI on an assumption that the grant set is stable between aghub runs.

There is no guard: `overwriteStatus` (add.ts:807-813, displayed at :826-833 / :1624-1631) only decorates the confirmation note, and `isInstalledProjectSkill` (skills.ts:182-194) filters the SOURCE clone, not the destination. Empirical: fixture with `.agent-hub/foo` = `description: OLD-MASTER`, links from `.agents/skills/foo`, `.claude/skills/foo`, `.grok/skills/foo`; ran `installSkillForAgent({name:'foo',path:src},'claude-code',{cwd:proj,mode:'symlink'})` where src = `description: NEW-FROM-NPX`. Disk after: `.agents/skills/foo` is `drwxrwxr-x` (a real dir) holding NEW-FROM-NPX; `.agent-hub/foo` still holds OLD-MASTER; `.claude/skills/foo` was REPOINTED to `../../.agents/skills/foo` (by `createSymlink`, installer.ts:224-234: lstat sees a symlink, `readlink` resolves to `.agent-hub/foo` ≠ the new target, so it `rm`s and recreates); `.grok/skills/foo` still points at `../../.agent-hub/foo` and `cat` through it printed OLD-MASTER. Reached by `add`, `install`, `i`, `a` (cli.ts:334-337). Global `-g` for a universal agent takes the same :359-360 write and returns at :365-372 before the symlink step, so the global Master is overwritten identically.

All eight project `.agents/skills` readers (codex, cline, warp, antigravity, copilot, gemini, amp, kimi) flip to the npx content while any agent aghub pointed straight at `.agent-hub` stays on the old content — precisely the silent behavioral failure this change is supposed to avoid. This does NOT exist today: today `.agents/skills/<name>` IS the Master, so an npx overwrite is seen by every referrer at once. The change introduces it. Because the migration links every existing skill, any user who runs `npx skills add` on a skill they also manage with aghub hits it on day one.

Add a regression test that builds exactly this fixture and asserts `doctor` reports it; without one the condition is invisible to CI. Also stop describing the `.agents/skills` entry as a Referrer aghub owns — npx will take it.

Either dedup must be dropped for the location view, or the refusal must name the shadowed path.

missed_areas.why_it_matters: The docs finding covers THIS repo's dogfood layout; the user-repo blast radius is different and unscanned. `.agents/skills` is an established convention users already deliberately commit or ignore (this repo commits 40 files under it). `.agent-hub` is brand new: every `aghub skill add -p` in any customer repo creates an untracked top-level directory that shows up in `git status` and that no template `.gitignore` knows about. Verified: this repo's `.gitignore` carries only `.agents/.aghub-mutation.lock` (line 47) — there is no `.agent-hub` rule anywhere, and nothing in the codebase writes one. Decide whether install writes/updates a `.gitignore` entry, and document the answer; a silent new dot-directory in someone's repo root is a support ticket.

missed_areas.why_it_matters: `grep -rn "agent-hub"` over the tree returns three hits, ALL in UPSTREAM.md (lines 29, 45, 183) where `agent-hub-revamp #282` names the upstream desktop UI architecture this fork deliberately did NOT adopt. contradictions.claim_a: crates/agents finding (opencode.rs): "global_skill_write_path has no fallback... The read fn has a fallback the write fn lacks, so the two disagree in exactly that case" — proposed fix: add `.unwrap_or_else(|| home.join(".config/opencode"))` to the write path so classify cannot return `Unsupported` and silently skip opencode.
contradictions.claim_b: Read the code: `config_dir_from` (opencode.rs:5-13) returns `None` ONLY when `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `home_dir()` are ALL absent — and `global_skills_paths()` (opencode.rs:100-110) early-returns an EMPTY vec on `let Some(home) = home_dir() else`. Read and write fail together; there is no case where one answers and the other does not.
contradictions.resolution: The finding is wrong and its fix is dead code — `.unwrap_or_else(|| home.join(".config/opencode"))` at opencode.rs:104-105 can never fire, because reaching that line already proves `home_dir()` is `Some`, which proves `config_dir()` is `Some`. Drop the proposed change. The real (and still open) opencode question is whether a machine that exports `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` gets its Referrer where the real binary scans — same class as the amp/kimi XDG divergence, and unlike that one it is symmetric here.

contradictions.claim_a: Core-prune finding (prune.rs:453): the fix is to append the Master store to `scope_skill_dirs`, and 'Consider also making top_level_skill_dirs honest about referrers, but adding the store is the necessary fix.'
contradictions.claim_b: API-prune finding (routes/skills.rs prune_lock_route): 'top_level_skill_dirs MUST accept a symlinked skill dir ... AND the scan set must include the .agent-hub Master store.'
contradictions.resolution: Both are required, for DIFFERENT states, and shipping only the core prescription leaves a hole. Store-in-scan is what keeps a zero-referrer skill alive in the lock. Symlink-aware `top_level_skill_dirs` is what keeps the disk set honest about referrer-only presence (an npx-era or hand-made skill whose only on-disk trace is a link in an agent dir). Safety fact that makes the second change cheap: the scanner's second half, `entry.path().join("SKILL.md").is_file()` (prune.rs:474), FOLLOWS the link, so a DANGLING referrer still fails the probe and cannot false-present. Pick both; say so explicitly, because 'adding the store is the necessary fix' reads as permission to skip the scanner half.

contradictions.claim_a: Linker finding (`link_agents_to_canonical`): 'Dedup `agent_skills_dirs` by `canonicalize_lenient` before the loop' so 8 shared-slot agents stop producing 1 `linked` + 7 `already_linked` rows.
contradictions.claim_b: API finding (`git_install_skills` / `install_skill_with_repo`): both routes zip the requested agent list POSITIONALLY against `report.agent_results`, which is sound only because `materialize_universal_master` emits exactly one row per entry of `target_agents`; a slot-dedupe would 'silently mis-attribute results to the wrong agents with no compile error'.
contradictions.resolution: Not a real conflict, but they must be read together or the linker fix breaks the API. Dedup belongs ONLY on the linker's `agent_skills_dirs` INPUT (a private list of paths); `materialize_universal_master` must keep emitting one `AgentInstallResult` per requested agent, folding `already_linked` parents into `linked_dirs` so all 8 report `installed: true`. Whoever does the dedup must add an assertion that `agent_results.len() == target_agents.len()`, or the positional zip in `crates/api` becomes a silent mis-attribution.

migration_hazards: A relative link created INSIDE `.agents/skills` pointing OUT of it is a NEW shape, and `relative_path` computes it lexically. `relative_path` (linker/mod.rs:106-135) walks `Component`s and emits `..` per remaining `from` component — a purely lexical operation. Today every `..` link points INTO `.agents/skills` from a sibling agent dir, so the trap never fires. After the change the Shared Referrer is `<root>/.agents/skills/foo -> ../../.agent-hub/foo`. If `<root>/.agents` is itself a symlink (dotfiles/stow setups do exactly this), the kernel resolves `..` from the REAL parent, not the lexical one, and the link dangles — this is precisely the failure root AGENTS.md forbids hand-rolled normalizers for, now on the WRITE path where `resolve_existing` is never consulted. Verified: no linker test constructs a symlinked `.agents` parent (`grep -rn symlink crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs` has no such fixture). Either resolve the `from` dir before computing the relative path, or use `LinkTarget::Absolute` for the Shared Referrer.

A fresh clone of THIS repo dangles, and the first `delete --yes` then prunes the committed lock. Verified via `git ls-files -s`: 40 tracked REGULAR files under `.agents/skills/` and 22 tracked symlinks (mode 120000) under `.claude/skills/` of the form `../../.agents/skills/<name>`, plus a committed root `skills-lock.json`. Committing the migration turns the 40 into symlinks into an untracked `.agent-hub/` → every clone gets 22 two-hop links resolving to nothing, and `prune_lock_for_scope` (run unconditionally by any executed `delete`) sees `file_type().is_dir() == false` for every entry and wipes the committed `skills-lock.json`, which lands in a commit. The AGENTS.md:62 finding names the decision but understates it as 'the repo's committed layout is not [safe]'.

Windows, two distinct hazards. (a) `LinkTarget`'s own doc (linker/mod.rs:29-35) states junctions ALWAYS resolve to absolute even when `Relative` is requested — so a project-scope `<root>/.agents/skills/<n>` stops being a portable, committable artifact on Windows the moment it becomes a junction; today it is a real directory that clones cleanly. (b) FLAG AS VERIFY-NOT-VERDICT (reasoning, not run here): git for Windows defaults `core.symlinks=false`, which materializes a committed symlink as a plain TEXT FILE containing the target string. A repo that commits `.agents/skills/<n>` as a link then hands Windows clones a file where 10 project agents expect a skill dir, and `Linker::link` sees a real occupant → `Conflict` forever with no repair path. Test on a Windows runner before committing any migrated layout.

There is a real directory at `.agents/skills/<name>` that aghub did NOT install — npx-written, hand-written, or committed by a teammate. It is not a Master aghub owns and must not be moved or deleted, yet it occupies the exact slot the 8 project (and 2 global) shared-slot agents now need for their Referrer. Every install/relink for those agents returns `Conflict` → `RESOURCE_EXISTS` until a human intervenes, and `install_universal` will already have claimed a fresh `.agent-hub/<name>` whose content is SHADOWED for all 10 project readers by the stale real dir — `check` then hashes a folder nobody reads. No finding proposes an answer for this set.

The copy-on-symlink-failure fallback is banned (linker/mod.rs:1-4: 'SM's iflow copy-mode is intentionally NOT ported: aghub bans copy as a skill-install outcome'), so a migration that cannot create the Referrer has NO degraded mode. Today a symlink failure for a NativeReader was harmless — the agent read the Master directly. After the change it is total skill loss for that agent, and the migration must therefore be transactional: if the Referrer cannot be created, the Master must not be moved out from under the real directory that is currently serving it.
new_risks_introduced: `apply-update` / `source sync` become SILENT no-ops after any npx write verb. The npx verification proves `installSkillForAgent`'s symlink mode does `cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir)` + `copyDirectory`, replacing `.agents/skills/<n>` with a REAL directory. aghub's resync targets come from `skill_root(skill)` → `canonical_path` → `.agent-hub/<n>`, so `stage_and_swap_dir` swaps content that the 8-10 `.agents/skills` readers no longer read, and reports success with a fresh lock hash. The npx report frames this as 'doctor should detect the shape'; the aghub-side consequence is that the update path reports green while delivering nothing. This cannot happen today, because the thing npx overwrites IS the Master.

Deleting the last Referrer for a skill leaves a Master that only the LOCK can find. Discovery cannot see `.agent-hub` (no descriptor reads it), so `installed_skill_roots_in`, `local_hashes_for_scope`, `prepare_locked_resync` and `GET /skills` all answer 'not installed' while `source list`/`source diff` (lock-driven) answer 'installed'. That divergence is not merely a reporting bug: it is a state aghub can enter with a single successful command and from which no aghub command can currently recover the Master except a hand-written path.

Every managed path now canonicalizes into ONE directory. `assert_contained` / `assert_strictly_contained` (removal.rs:130-158) canonicalize the target before the root test, so after `.agent-hub` is added to `universal_master_roots` every Referrer in every agent dir resolves INTO an allow-listed root. The allow-list stops distinguishing 'a path aghub may delete' from 'a path that merely points at one' — it was previously a location test, and it silently becomes a resolution test. Verified it does not bite the current callers (`single_agent_keep_reason` and `plan_copy_removal` only ever receive real directories), but any future caller that hands it a link inherits a permissive answer with no compile-time signal.

`.agent-hub` is resolved from `dirs::home_dir()` with no env override, while `set_skills_path_override` — the ONLY test isolation hook for skill paths — cannot redirect it. That is the same shape as the pre-existing `.agents/skills` pollution trap, but it now applies to a second directory that no existing test teardown enumerates, and it applies to the path holding the ONLY physical copy of every skill.
must_decide_before_coding: Is the migration worklist LOCK-DRIVEN or DISK-DRIVEN? Not asked anywhere in the 60+ open questions, and it decides the answer to the whole 'foreign real directory' class. Lock-driven (migrate only names in `~/.skill-lock.json` / `skills-lock.json`) leaves every npx-written, hand-written or committed real dir sitting in the slot the shared-slot agents need → permanent `Conflict`. Disk-driven (migrate every real dir under `.agents/skills`) moves content aghub never installed into a directory aghub owns and reference-counts. Pick one and state explicitly what happens to the other set.

Who runs the migration on a host that has no CLI? The remote VM (crates/remote) and any standalone `aghub-api` deployment run the server binary only. If migration is a CLI startup step, those hosts never migrate and every install for a shared-slot agent fails forever.

Does the Shared Referrer use `LinkTarget::Relative` or `Absolute` at project scope? Relative is what the current project path does, but it is the first `..` link aghub creates pointing OUT of `.agents/skills`, computed lexically — a symlinked `.agents` parent dangles it. Absolute is safe but non-portable and matches what Windows junctions do anyway.

Does the migration create ONE Shared Referrer at `.agents/skills/<name>`, or per-agent Referrers for the agents actually recorded in the lock? The stated policy ('一律建立 .agents/skills/<name> link, 行為與今天完全一致') delivers behavior parity but gives the user an all-or-nothing grant for 5 global / 8 project agents — so the promised '之後手動收緊' is not per-agent for exactly the agents the change was meant to separate. Per-agent Referrers cost more disk links but make the follow-up capability real.

Does aghub write a `.gitignore` entry for `.agent-hub` in a project root, and does THIS repo commit `.agent-hub/` or exempt itself from migration? Both answers are needed before the first commit that moves a Master, because they are the difference between a clean clone and 22 dangling links plus a wiped lock.
